central_topic: Predicting an LLM's full binary benchmark score and model ranking from 8, 16, or 32 source-selected items using group-aware score-covariance design and a ridge/Rasch-residual profile blend, with limited generalization evidence on held-out benchmark cases.
core_methods: Fixed nested item selection by squared conditional covariance with the source full score divided by conditional item variance, using a low-rank pivoted factorization
Equal source-group weighting for acquisition, Rasch fitting, particle priors, and grouped tuning losses
Ridge full-score regression with shrinkage toward the training-source mean
Rasch-shrunk source response profiles with discrete ability-offset particles and Bernoulli posterior updating
Exact observed-score contribution plus posterior expected unobserved-score contribution
Source-only group-disjoint tuning of a convex linear/profile-posterior blend
comparators: Response-vector clustering anchors and weighted score estimation: Anchor Points
IRT-assisted benchmark compression and score estimation: tinyBenchmarks and metabench
Adaptive evaluation acquisition, as a related selection family rather than an implemented target-adaptive policy
Reference-instance prediction of unseen model performance: 100 instances is all you need
Score-targeted experimental design versus representation-diversity selection
Uniform item sampling and raw sample means; uniform selection with the learned predictor; source-mean, constant, copy, and IRT controls
benchmarks: Development/search: ARC-Challenge, IFEval, MMLU-Pro, from staged Open LLM Leaderboard matrices
Final: bbh, gpqa, musr, openllm_math, from staged Open LLM Leaderboard matrices
Final: commonsense, gsm, legalbench, math, med_qa, mmlu, from staged HELM matrices
Pinned benchmark-prediction score-matrix snapshot: 55faff496947789f94e6b5908c77cbc3e84f81ad; evaluation uses staged, filtered fixed item universes
result_driven_themes: Limited generalization from development benchmarks to held-out benchmark cases: the selected method's final retained MAE is worse than its search MAE, and final evaluation did not qualify
Selection and estimation must be separated: uniform selection with the learned predictor has lower retained final MAE than score-targeted selection, whereas the ordering reverses in search
Raw subset averaging and learned full-score prediction are distinct: the no_calibration mode returns the observed mean rather than merely removing an affine calibration layer
Model-family dependence motivates group-disjoint source tuning, but opaque groups and heuristic family metadata do not certify true ancestry or architecture transfer
Ranking correlations and retained MAE are descriptive evidence, not proof of calibrated uncertainty, statistical superiority, or a diagnosed cause of final non-qualification

queries.query: Anchor Points: Benchmarking Models with Much Fewer Examples
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for response-vector clustering and weighted anchor estimates; directly contextualizes the recorded anchor comparator without equating that comparator to an audited official reproduction.

queries.query: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference combining anchors and IRT; essential context for the recorded IRT comparator and the implemented Rasch-based score predictor.

queries.query: metabench A Sparse Benchmark of Reasoning and Knowledge in LLMs
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for IRT-informed item selection and learned full-score prediction; contrasts information-based selection with the implemented full-score covariance objective.

queries.query: Active Evaluation Acquisition for Efficient LLM Benchmarking
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for learned adaptive acquisition; establishes the boundary between target-adaptive selection and this run's fixed source-only nested prefixes, not an unrun head-to-head comparison.

queries.query: c-optimal experimental design prediction linear functional
queries.rationale: The selector targets conditional uncertainty in a scalar full score rather than general representation diversity. Classical linear-functional design is the relevant methodological neighborhood; exact c-optimality of this implementation is not claimed.

queries.query: latent class Rasch models local dependence item responses
queries.rationale: The selected configuration mixes Rasch-shrunk empirical source profiles and discrete ability offsets. Mixture psychometrics and local-dependence literature contextualize that representation and its conditional-independence limitations without claiming equivalence to a particular published model.

queries.query: 100 instances is all you need: predicting the success of a new LLM on unseen data by testing on a few instances
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for predicting unobserved instance outcomes from reference-instance responses; directly relevant to source-profile inference and the observed/unobserved score decomposition.

queries.query: grouped cross-validation hierarchical dependent data prediction assessment
queries.rationale: Group-disjoint source tuning is implemented, while the search/final selection-control reversal motivates caution about generalization. Classical dependent-data validation is relevant; the reversal alone does not establish family shift or a causal explanation.

queries.query: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models HELM
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for the source evaluation framework underlying six final benchmark matrices; cite dataset context without treating framework-wide claims or the raw upstream release as properties of the staged fixed item universes.

queries.query: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 Fourrier Habib Lozovskaya Szafer Wolf
queries.rationale: Permitted starter reference for the leaderboard context underlying the development matrices and four final matrices; future retrieval must verify benchmark-specific provenance rather than assume every staged case is an official v2 component.
